skill.name: python-executor
skill.description: Run Python code through the inference.sh belt CLI with common data, scraping, image, video, document, and 3D processing libraries available in a sandboxed runtime.
skill.summary: Run sandboxed Python scripts for data work, automation, and media processing through inference.sh.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The Markdown backtick findings are mostly documentation false positives, but the real belt examples execute user-supplied Python through an external service. Network access is an intended feature through HTTP examples and external service links. No prompt injection text was found, but the skill remains high risk because it enables broad remote code execution.

remediation.issue: Broad remote Python execution through belt
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before every belt run and show the exact Python code, network targets, timeout, and output paths.

remediation.issue: External service dependency for code execution
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that code and inputs are sent to inference.sh, and warn users not to include secrets or private datasets.
Document that HTTP requests should be limited to approved domains and reviewed before execution.
Separate npx installation steps from execution examples and require manual approval for installing related skills.

content.value_statement: Agents often need Python execution without local dependency setup. This skill routes scripts to an inference.sh sandbox with common scientific, web, and media libraries.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python snippets through the belt CLI against the infsh/python-executor app.
Supports data analysis with pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly.
Runs web scraping and API examples with requests, BeautifulSoup, Selenium, and Playwright.
Creates output files in an outputs directory for charts, images, videos, PDFs, and 3D models.
Offers a high-memory variant for larger CPU-only workloads.
Documents timeouts, output capture, and working directory inputs for execution control.
limitations: Requires the external inference.sh belt CLI and an authenticated account.
Execution is CPU-only and does not include GPU or dedicated machine learning runtimes.
Network behavior depends on the submitted Python code and the remote sandbox policy.
It is not suitable for secrets, private datasets, or unreviewed code without explicit user consent.

use_cases.title: Analyze Small Datasets
use_cases.description: Process tabular data and generate charts without installing Python packages locally.

use_cases.title: Create Media Assets
use_cases.description: Generate images, videos, PDFs, or 3D files from short Python scripts.

use_cases.title: Automate API Checks
use_cases.description: Run short scripts that call approved APIs and summarize the returned data.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Calculation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a short Python script that calculates the requested values and returns the printed result.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a CSV File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to inspect this CSV, summarize key columns, and create a chart file in the outputs directory.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Document Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to create a PDF or image from my provided content and return the generated output file.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled API Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to call only the approved API endpoint, transform the response, and save a concise report file.

output_examples.input: Analyze sales by person and create a bar chart.
output_examples.output: A printed summary of totals and an attached chart image saved from the sandbox run.

output_examples.input: Resize and convert an uploaded image for web use.
output_examples.output: A processed image file plus a short note with final dimensions and file format.

output_examples.input: Fetch public profile data from an approved API and summarize it.
output_examples.output: A concise text summary with selected fields from the API response.

best_practices: Review Python code before execution, especially when it performs network requests or file writes.
Keep inputs small, explicit, and free of secrets or private credentials.
Set a practical timeout and save expected artifacts under the outputs directory.
anti_patterns: Do not run code copied from untrusted sources without inspection.
Do not send confidential files, tokens, or customer data to the remote sandbox.
Do not use this skill for interactive programs, long-running jobs, or GPU workloads.

faq.question: Does this skill run Python locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh belt CLI to run Python in an external sandboxed app.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: The examples include HTTP and API requests, so users should review all network access before execution.

faq.question: Can it return generated files?
faq.answer: Yes. Files saved in the outputs directory are described as automatically returned.

faq.question: Is it safe for secrets?
faq.answer: No. Avoid secrets and private data because execution is delegated to an external service.

faq.question: Does it support GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes a CPU-only Python 3.10 environment.
